name: Calendar manager M0
objective:
Implement milestone M0 of the Agenda/Calendar manager as specified in design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md (§16 "M0 — global foundations"), committing NOTHING beyond what the design specifies.

Context the workers must read first:
- design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md — §3 (domain model: Calendar scope/owner/audience, CalendarEvent, Occurrence), §4.1 (global storage layout, month shards), §4.3 (CompanyStore conventions), §5 (backend API contract), §5.4 (additive Chat fields), §11.1 (per-request ACL), Appendix A (exact file map).
- design/06-calendar/03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json — version-2 canonical dataset in API shape with expected_filters / expected_reminders assertions.
- design/06-calendar/02-prototype/index.html — the verified interactive prototype: source of truth for the UI layout and behaviour.

Locked decisions: D1 the calendar store is GLOBAL ($CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH, default /home/codx-junior/calendar) and projects are only a FILTER; D2 calendars have scope private|team|workspace|system|external with per-request ACL; D3 meets are scheduled from the calendar (M1, out of M0); D4 Google/ICS is out of scope.

M0 scope = global path + models + atomic JSON store + service with ACL and filtered query + /api/calendar router + additive Chat fields + Pinia store + CalendarView (month/week/day/agenda, project filter, scope-grouped sidebar, event editor) + wiring + backend tests. M0 has NO new dependency, NO background work, NO recurrence expansion (recurrence fields exist but expansion is M3), NO meet scheduling (M1), NO reminders thread (M2).

Hard constraints:
- Additive only to existing shared files (globals.py, db.py, api.js, store/index.js, router/index.ts, apps.js, appComponentsMap.js). Never rename or remove existing fields, endpoints or components.
- Nothing in the calendar router may use settings.codx_path as a data root.
- Existing test suite must keep passing; tests must never write to the real /home/codx-junior/calendar.

Acceptance (from §16, verified against the fixture): user "marta" never sees the Work/Personal private calendars; a team calendar is readable by a reader member and not writable by it; the project filter reproduces expected_filters exactly (9 / 2 / 1, total 12, OR semantics); fixture-driven backend tests are green.

steps.title: M0 backend foundation: global path, models, atomic JSON store
steps.objective:
Build the M0 backend foundation exactly as specified. Read design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md §3 (domain model), §4.1 (global layout + month shards), §4.3 (CompanyStore conventions), §5.4 (Chat fields), and Appendix A before writing code.

1) api/codx/junior/globals.py — add, in the existing style and beside the other global folder constants:
   CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH = os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH", "/home/codx-junior/calendar")
   Do not change any existing constant.

2) New package api/codx/junior/calendar/__init__.py exporting the public names (Calendar, CalendarEvent, Occurrence, CalendarStore, ...).

3) api/codx/junior/calendar/model.py — pydantic models, following the naming/style of api/codx/junior/meets/model.py and api/codx/junior/kanban/model.py:
   - ReminderRule {channel: str = "popup", minutes_before: int = 10}
   - CalendarMember {user: str, role: "owner"|"writer"|"reader"}
   - Calendar — every field of §3.1: id, name, color, description="", scope (Literal private|team|workspace|system|external), owner, audience: Optional[dict]=None, timezone="UTC", read_only=False, provider="local", default_reminders: List[ReminderRule], members: List[CalendarMember], visible=True, order=0, created_at, updated_at. Property is_read_only = read_only or scope in ("system","external").
   - Recurrence — fields present but UNUSED in M0 (RRULE string + overrides list); declare it so M3 is additive.
   - CalendarEvent — every field of §3.2 with the §3.2 invariants 1-6 documented in the docstring; calendar_ids non-empty + deduplicated (validator), project_id Optional[str], start/end ISO strings, all_day, timezone, recurrence Optional, reminders, status, visibility, source, refs, guests, created_by, created_at, updated_at, revision=1.
   - Occurrence — §3.3 including calendar_id (singular, the colour carrier), is_recurring_instance, original_start, overdue, read_only.
   - Payloads: CalendarCreate, CalendarUpdate (all fields optional), EventQuery {calendar_ids?, from_, to, projects?, q?, sources?, include_hidden?} using alias "from" for from_, EventCreate, EventUpdate.

4) api/codx/junior/calendar/store.py — CalendarStore with the exact conventions of api/codx/junior/company/store.py: create dirs on demand, flock around writes, atomic tmp file + os.replace, tolerate missing/corrupt JSON (log a warning, return empty, never raise). Root from globals.CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH, overridable via constructor arg for tests. Layout per §4.1: calendars.json, events/<YYYY-MM>.json, delivered.json, prefs/<username>.json. Methods at least: list_calendars / get_calendar / save_calendar / delete_calendar, list_events_month / list_events_range (reads the requested months PLUS one month either side, per §4.4) / get_event / save_event / delete_event, get_prefs / save_prefs, read_delivered / write_delivered. Event shard key = start month in UTC.

5) api/codx/junior/db.py — ADD to the Chat model, additive and defaulted so existing task files load unchanged: calendar_ids: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list), scheduled_start: Optional[str] = None, scheduled_end: Optional[str] = None, all_day: bool = False. Change nothing else; due_date keeps its deadline meaning.

Do not create service.py, the router, or any client file — those are the next steps.

Acceptance: a short runnable smoke check proves it works — point CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH at a temp dir, save+reload a calendar and an event, assert the event lands in the right month shard and that a corrupt shard returns [] instead of raising. Paste the command and its output. Also confirm `python -c "import codx.junior.db"` still imports.
steps.acceptance: Model and store import cleanly; the temp-dir round-trip smoke check passes (calendar + event persisted, correct month shard, corrupt file tolerated); Chat still imports with the four new defaulted fields; globals.py gains only the new constant.

steps.title: M0 service (ACL + filtered query) and /api/calendar router
steps.objective:
Add the service layer and the HTTP router on top of the foundation from the previous step. Read design/06-calendar/01-analysis.md §5 (full API contract), §5.2 (projects[] filter semantics), §5.3 (errors + collection events), §11.1 (ACL table) and api/codx/junior/api/meets.py + management.py for the request.state.codx_junior_session pattern, then write:

1) api/codx/junior/calendar/service.py — CalendarService(store, viewer, settings?) with:
   - ACL. can_view(calendar): private -> owner == viewer only; team -> audience members contain viewer (audience = {kind:"team", project, name, members[]}); workspace/system/external -> every authenticated user. can_write(calendar): owner or writer member; workspace requires an installation admin (reuse the existing user/role resolution, do not invent one); system/external never writable. Never leak a private calendar's name, colour or events to a non-owner — filter at the calendar list, not only at the event level.
   - query(EventQuery): resolve visible calendars -> apply projects[] AFTER visibility and BEFORE any expansion, with exactly these semantics: absent or [] = no project filtering; ["personal"] matches project_id is None; several ids = OR. Return {range, calendars, projects, occurrences[], counts{by_calendar,by_source,by_project}, warnings[], truncated_projects[]}. One occurrence per event; calendar_id = first visible membership (colour carrier), full calendar_ids kept. No recurrence expansion in M0 — a recurring event yields ONE occurrence at its stored start.
   - create/update/delete event with the §3.2 invariants enforced: non-empty deduplicated calendar_ids, all ids must resolve (unknown_calendar), end > start unless all_day, system/external-only write -> 409 read_only_calendar, revision increments on every write, If-Match mismatch -> 409 revision_mismatch. delete_calendar -> 409 calendar_in_use unless move_to given.
   - prefs per user (prefs/<username>.json): hidden calendars, order, week_start; and projects() returning [{project_id, name, role}] for the filter bar.

2) api/codx/junior/api/calendar.py — module-level `router = APIRouter()` (auto-discovered and mounted at /api by api/codx/junior/api/__init__.py). Implement every route of §5.1 and §5.2 at the documented paths and methods, including POST /api/calendar/events/query as the main read, GET /calendars/{id}/share, GET /calendar/projects, GET+PUT /calendar/prefs. Use HTTPException with the §5.3 string error codes. After each successful write, emit_collection_event with a new COLLECTION_CALENDAR_EVENTS constant added to events/collection_events.py (additive, plus its COLLECTIONS entry).

3) Hard constraint: the data root is globals.CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH. Nothing in this router may use settings.codx_path as a storage root; request.state.codx_junior_session is used for authentication/identity only.

Do not write tests or client files.

Acceptance: the app imports and the calendar routes are registered at the documented paths — print the route table (method + path) from the FastAPI app and paste it; confirm no occurrence of settings.codx_path in the two new files.
steps.acceptance: App imports; printed route table matches §5.1/§5.2 exactly (method + path); ACL helpers covered by reading the code (private invisible to non-owner, team reader cannot write, system/external read-only); projects[] semantics implemented as absent/[] = all, personal = null, several = OR; zero settings.codx_path usage in calendar/service.py and api/calendar.py.

steps.title: M0 backend tests driven by the v2 fixture
steps.objective:
Write api/tests/test_calendar_store.py and api/tests/test_calendar_service.py (pytest, matching the style of the existing tests under api/tests/).

Seed each test from design/06-calendar/03-fixtures/calendar-fixture.json — do not retype the dataset by hand. Load the fixture, write it into a pytest tmp_path store (constructor arg or monkeypatched CODX_JUNIOR_CALENDAR_PATH); NEVER touch the real /home/codx-junior/calendar.

Cover at minimum:
1) Store: round-trip calendar and event; month shard file naming; list_events_range reads the ±1 month overlap; corrupt JSON tolerated; concurrent write does not corrupt the file (two sequential writes with flock).
2) Visibility ACL: viewer "marta" does not see the Work/Personal private calendars nor their events (assert absence of ids AND absence of titles); the owner does see them; a team calendar is visible to a reader and a reader's write is rejected; a system/external calendar is visible but read_only.
3) Project filter: assert expected_filters from the fixture verbatim — projects ["codx-junior-platform"] -> 9 occurrences with by_source {native:2, meet:5, task:1, orchestration:1}; the second filter -> 2; ["personal"] -> 1; unfiltered total 12; and that combining two project ids is an OR (sums, never intersects).
4) Write paths: unknown_calendar, read_only_calendar, revision_mismatch (If-Match with a stale revision), calendar_in_use without move_to, and that move_to rehomes the events.

If a test exposes a real bug in the service or the store, fix it minimally and say exactly what you changed and why in your result.

Acceptance: run the suite the way this project runs pytest (inspect api/pyproject.toml / api/Makefile for the configured command) and paste the summary line plus the pass count. Zero failures, zero errors, and no writes outside tmp dirs. Also confirm the pre-existing tests still pass.
steps.acceptance: Both new test files pass with 0 failures / 0 errors in the project's configured pytest invocation; the assertions reproduce expected_filters (9 / 2 / 1, total 12, OR semantics) and the marta privacy rule verbatim from the fixture; no test writes to /home/codx-junior/calendar; pre-existing tests still green.

steps.title: M0 UI: CalendarView, grids, sidebar, project filter, store and wiring
steps.objective:
Build the M0 client, porting the verified prototype design/06-calendar/02-prototype/index.html (open it first — it is the visual and behavioural source of truth) onto the real stack. Read client/src/store/planning.js, client/src/api/modules/meets.js, client/src/api/api.js, client/src/store/index.js, client/src/config/apps.js, appComponentsMap.js and router/index.ts to copy the existing conventions exactly.

1) client/src/api/modules/calendar.js — thin module over the §5 endpoints (calendars CRUD + share, projects, prefs, events query/create/get/update/delete).
2) client/src/store/calendar.js — Pinia store like planning.js: state (calendars, occurrences, counts, range, projects, activeProjects, view, cursor, loading, error), getters (visibleCalendars grouped by scope: My calendars / Shared with me / codx-junior / Other, filteredOccurrences), actions (loadCalendars, loadProjects, loadRange, setView, shift, toggleCalendar, setProjectFilter, createEvent, updateEvent, deleteEvent, loadPrefs, savePrefs). The project filter is multi-select and ORs, defaulting to All; persist the choice via prefs.
3) client/src/views/CalendarView.vue + client/src/components/calendar/* as listed in Appendix A — month grid (chips, max N per day then +more), week grid (hour rows, positioned blocks, today line), day view (the cursor day, correct weekday label), agenda list, scope-grouped sidebar with colour toggles, project filter bar with a filtered/total counter, event editor modal (title, calendars multi-select, project selector, start/end, all-day, reminders, guests) and a popover on chip click. Multi-calendar chips show extra-membership badges.
4) Wiring, all additive: apps.js 'calendar' entry, appComponentsMap.js lazy component, router/index.ts route '/:projectName/calendar', api.js calendarModule + lazy getter, store/index.js calendar module.

Constraints: no new npm dependency, no CDN; follow the existing design tokens (--codx-primary #cc0099) and component style already in client/src; the server returns occurrences already expanded, so the client does no date maths beyond formatting.

Acceptance: the client builds — run the project's own build/lint script (check client/package.json) and paste the command and result. List every file created and every existing file modified. If the build reports errors that already exist on HEAD, say so explicitly and prove it.
steps.acceptance: Client build (or the project's configured lint/typecheck) succeeds and the command + result are reported; every Appendix A client file exists; apps.js / appComponentsMap.js / router/index.ts / api.js / store/index.js changes are additive only; no new npm dependency in package.json; a route /:projectName/calendar resolves to CalendarView.
